SMART PLUG
SYSTEM
Self-Turning Off Plug · Design Thinking · Embedded Systems
The Idea
Devices left plugged in unnecessarily lead to energy waste, higher electricity bills, and potential safety risks. Instead of treating this as just a technical build, the approach was through design thinking — focusing on real user behavior: forgetfulness during busy routines and lack of awareness about standby power.
The Solution
A smart plug that automatically cuts off power based on user-defined conditions such as time or inactivity. It balances automation with control — users can override or customize settings easily. Automation that works quietly without demanding attention.
Goals Achieved
  • Reduce unnecessary energy consumption
  • Improve household electrical safety
  • Simplify everyday device interactions
  • Integrate technology invisibly into daily life
Components Used
Microcontroller
Relay Module
User Input Controls
Power Supply Unit
LED Indicators
Enclosure / Housing
GESTURE
ROBOT
Wireless Control · Human-Machine Interaction · Motor Systems
The Concept
A more natural way to interact with machines — controlling a robotic vehicle using hand gestures instead of traditional controllers. The goal: bridge the gap between human motion and machine response, translating physical gestures into real-time commands.
How It Works
A dual-unit system: a motion-sensing hand unit captures orientation and tilt, while the vehicle unit receives and executes commands wirelessly. Hand gestures are detected via a motion sensor tracking acceleration and rotation, mapped to directional commands, and transmitted via Bluetooth. An H-bridge driver handles motor control.
Key Highlights
  • Real-time gesture-based control — no traditional controller
  • Bluetooth wireless communication
  • Modular transmitter + receiver architecture
  • H-bridge motor driver for smooth navigation
  • Stable I2C sensor communication
  • Safe power distribution design
